Competency-based programs set no hour count and must state the competencies and how each is tested. Hybrid programs combine minimum hours with demonstrated competency. Completers get a certificate from the Registration Agency; competency and hybrid programs may issue interim credentials.

name: Piaget's stages of cognitive development
notes: Read from Wikipedia as a pointer; first 100,000 characters of the page. Critiques recorded there: development is more gradual than stages imply and Piaget described this as decalage; Lourenco and Machado 1996; infants show object knowledge at 3 months in Baillargeon's habituation studies; performance varies by domain; Vygotsky and Bruner give language and culture a larger role; cross-cultural results shift when procedures fit the local language; neo-Piagetian accounts tie stage change to working memory and processing efficiency.

name: Theory-of-mind scale for preschoolers
notes: 75 children aged 2 years 11 months to 6 years 6 months, 7 tasks. Responses formed a Guttman scale: a child who passed a later task had passed the earlier ones. The abstract does not list the tasks; the five-step order stored here is from memory. Wellman, Cross and Watson 2001 pooled 178 false-belief studies and found a consistent shift across the preschool years, with age, country and task factors explaining 55% of variance.

name: Development of emotion regulation from co-regulation to self-regulation
body: Developmental psychology literature, for example Kopp 1989 and Gross
notes: No single published staged standard was found. Sequence recalled from memory. Compas et al. 2017 pooled 212 studies with 80,850 participants on coping and emotion regulation against symptoms in childhood and adolescence.

name: Kohlberg's stages of moral development
notes: Read from Wikipedia as a pointer. From the 1958 Chicago dissertation on ages 10 to 16, male participants. The page gives no age per stage. Critiques: Gilligan 1982, the scale centres justice and omits care; Walker 1984, a meta-analysis found no significant sex difference; Snarey 1985, 45 cross-cultural studies support the early sequence and find bias toward urban, middle-class societies at the upper stages; Gibbs et al. 2007; Haidt 2001, reasoning often follows intuition; Krebs and Denton 2005, the model does not explain everyday moral decisions; no statistical support for stage 6.

name: Enhancing and Practicing Executive Function Skills with Children from Infancy to Adolescence
body: Center on the Developing Child, Harvard University
notes: Six age bands. The activities sit in PDFs that were not fetched. Best and Miller 2010: inhibition, working memory and shifting emerge in the first years and strengthen through childhood and adolescence on different trajectories.

name: National Physical Education Standards
notes: Four standards: motor skills, knowledge of movement and fitness, social skills, personal skills and engagement. Indicators by grade span PreK-2, 3-5, 6-8 and 9-12. Released March 2024; the 2013 edition had five standards.

name: Fundamental movement phase of motor development
body: David Gallahue and John Ozmun, Understanding Motor Development
notes: From memory. Barnett et al. 2016 reviewed correlates of gross motor competence at ages 3 to 18 across object control, locomotor and stability skills. Robinson et al. 2015: motor competence is linked to physical activity, fitness and weight status.

name: Tanner stages of pubertal development
body: W. A. Marshall and J. M. Tanner
notes: Boys' paper fetched: 228 boys, mixed longitudinal data, British sample of the 1950s and 1960s. The girls' paper, 1969, has no abstract in PubMed. Five stages per characteristic. Ages have shifted earlier in later cohorts.

name: National Health Education Standards
notes: Eight standards with performance indicators for PreK-2, 3-5, 6-8 and 9-12. Released March 2024; replaces the 2007 edition.

notes: 2025 civics test for applications filed on or after 2025-10-20.

name: Andragogy: assumptions about adult learners
notes: Read from Wikipedia as a pointer. Six assumptions. Evidence: the page reports a lack of research on whether these principles serve adults better than good teaching in general. Critiques: Kidd 1978, learning principles hold across the lifespan; Hanson 1996, differences follow context, culture and power more than age; Merriam 2001, adults do not always want self-direction; Rachal 2002, Knowles's own course limited learner choice. Knowles later described a continuum from pedagogy to andragogy.

name: WorkAdvance sectoral advancement model
body: MDRC; NYC Center for Economic Opportunity
notes: RCT, 2,564 adults, four providers in New York City, Tulsa and Greater Cleveland, enrolment June 2011 to June 2013. Four components over up to two years. Follow-up in 2017 and 2018: Per Scholas raised average earnings in both years; St. Nicks Alliance, Madison Strategies Group and Towards Employment showed no significant effect; the pooled sample showed a gain. MDRC's 2020 summary puts the Per Scholas gain above $6,000 a year, 20%. Katz et al. 2022: sectoral programmes raise earnings 12% to 34% after training.

name: Year Up
body: Year Up United; evaluated by Abt Associates for OPRE in the PACE project

name: Sector Strategies for Success
notes: Evidence summary. Per Scholas: IT credential receipt up more than 46%, annual earnings up over $6,000, 20%. Year Up: quarterly earnings up 53% at the earlier follow-up. Project QUEST: annual earnings up $5,239, 18%. HPOG: shorter trainings led to lower wages than longer ones.

name: WIA Adult and Dislocated Worker Programs Gold Standard Evaluation
body: Mathematica for the US Department of Labor
notes: Random assignment in 28 local areas. Over 30 months, intensive services raised earnings by $3,300 to $7,100 per customer, 7% to 20%. Training funded by the programmes showed no positive earnings impact within 30 months; the evidence is inconclusive.

name: Evaluation of the Trade Adjustment Assistance Program
body: Social Policy Research Associates and Mathematica for the US Department of Labor
notes: Synthesis by D'Amico and Schochet of more than a dozen reports, with a matched comparison group of unemployment insurance claimants. The landing page gives no impact estimate. From memory: participants earned less than the comparison group over four years, with the gap closing late.

name: The PLA Boost
notes: 72 institutions, more than 230,000 adult students. 49% of adults with prior learning credit completed a credential against 27% without. With controls, credit raised completion by 17%. The report was revised in December 2020 for a data-matching error; the revision was not fetched.

name: Osher Lifelong Learning Institutes
notes: 125 university-based programmes for adults aged 50 and over, one or more in every state and DC. Non-credit courses with no exams or grades. First grant in 2001 to the University of Southern Maine.

name: ACTIVE: Advanced Cognitive Training for Independent and Vital Elderly
body: ACTIVE Study Group, funded by NIA and NINR
notes: RCT, 2,832 adults living independently in six cities, mean age 73.6. Ten sessions of memory, reasoning or speed-of-processing training against a no-contact control; four booster sessions at 11 and 35 months for a random subset. Results at 2, 5, 10 and 20 years are on the progression rows.

name: Technology use among adults 65 and older
notes: Survey of early 2021: 61% of adults 65 and over own a smartphone, 75% use the internet, 45% use social media, 44% own a tablet. The smartphone gap to ages 18 to 29 fell from 53 points in 2012 to 35 in 2021. Hunsaker and Hargittai 2018 review access, skills and inequality in older adults' internet use.

notes: Ten steps. Figures on the page: 70% to 80% of pre-retirement income needed; Social Security replaces about 40% on average; IRA limit $7,500 a year with more from age 50.

name: Chronic Disease Self-Management Program
body: Self-Management Resource Center; developed at Stanford by Kate Lorig
notes: Six weekly sessions of 2.5 hours, 8 to 14 people, two trained leaders, one or both peers with a chronic condition. Workshop last updated 2020. Evidence: Lorig et al. 1999 RCT, at 6 months more exercise, better symptom management and communication with physicians, less fatigue and disability, fewer hospital days, no change in pain or psychological well-being; Ory et al. 2013 national study, gains held to 12 months with fewer emergency visits; Brady et al. 2013 meta-analysis of 23 studies, small significant gains in exercise, symptom management and psychological health at 4 to 6 months, part held at 9 to 12. Stanford origin from memory.

name: Advance Care Planning: Advance Directives for Health Care
notes: Content reviewed 2022-10-31. Brinkman-Stoppelenburg et al. 2014 reviewed 113 studies of advance care planning, 95% observational and 81% from the United States.

name: Metacognition and self-regulation, Teaching and Learning Toolkit
notes: Average impact of eight additional months of progress over a year. Evidence security rated high across 355 studies, with one padlock lost because many studies were not independently evaluated. Pupils are taught strategies to plan, monitor and evaluate their learning on challenging tasks in the normal curriculum.

name: Development of metacognition from childhood to adulthood
notes: Schneider 2008: early theory of mind predicts later declarative metacognitive knowledge through language; declarative knowledge rises steadily through childhood and adolescence, driven by strategy knowledge; self-control shows age trends and monitoring shows little. Kuhn 2000: the progression ends in metaknowing skills that many adults do not master. Ages on the rows are approximations.

name: Zimmerman's social cognitive model of self-regulated learning

name: Study skills and learning strategy programmes
notes: Hattie, Biggs and Purdie 1996: 51 studies; training works best in context, in the target subject, with active learners and metacognitive awareness; only simple mnemonic training transfers out of context. Crede and Kuncel 2008: across 344 samples and 72,431 college students, study habits and motivation predict grades about as well as admission tests and prior grades. Dignath and Buttner 2008 and Donker et al. 2014: records confirmed, abstracts not retrieved.

name: Deliberate practice
body: K. Anders Ericsson, Ralf Krampe and Clemens Tesch-Romer

notes: A fluent elder and a younger adult work in the language for up to 300 hours a year, for up to three years, on a 9,000 dollar grant. 10 to 20 teams a year. Start year 1992 or 1993 by search results.

name: Farmer field schools
